provenance: Retrospective analysis, actual archived render extracts and selected owner feedback. Not contemporaneous hidden reasoning or a controlled user experiment.

cases.title: Make the brief observable
cases.observation: The first TV pass still uses bounded content regions. The later composition gives the word and orange gesture the frame.
cases.decision: Translate TV-friendly into free-standing type, a single focal action and open negative space.
cases.why: The requested presentation is viewed at playback speed. Layout should communicate priority before the viewer starts reading.
cases.outtake: Keep the boxed version as a direction study. It helped expose the mismatch; it is not a universal rule that cards never work.
cases.lesson: Convert a style adjective into criteria that another model or designer can evaluate.

cases.title: Give the first point time to land
cases.observation: The owner asked for slower, progressive first points and faster introductions later in the cut.
cases.decision: Introduce points separately with opacity ramps and larger focus; redistribute time instead of uniformly slowing every scene.
cases.why: A viewer needs time to identify the visual grammar before the edit accelerates.
cases.outtake: The quicker opening is retained as the pacing counterexample. A still alone cannot prove timing; use the linked clips.
cases.lesson: Specify onset, duration, hold and where the time is recovered.

cases.title: Show the causal chain, not a workflow label
cases.observation: A capture/configuration view requires the viewer to infer the automation. The reconstructed scene draws a trigger, then its branches.
cases.decision: Use the real BOM-edit example; grow actions slowly first, widen the camera, then accelerate the later branches.
cases.why: The animation makes cause and effect visible in sequence, with the newest action as the focus.
cases.outtake: Keep the setup screen as source evidence, not as the final hero demonstration. Configured actions are not proof that a fresh run occurred.
cases.lesson: Teach the system to explain behavior spatially while retaining the evidence boundary.

cases.title: Make the BOM relationship legible
cases.observation: The original quantity/cost capture proves an interaction. A full BOM needs a different visual hierarchy to explain how lines accumulate.
cases.decision: Keep the verified 32 × 475.50 = 15,216.00 example, then fold it into an orderly full list and planned total.
cases.why: A coherent calculation-to-list transition reduces the amount of UI the viewer must decode.
cases.outtake: The screen recording remains reference proof. The later visual is explicitly a cleaned-up representation, not a newly saved transaction.
cases.lesson: Simplify presentation without inventing responsiveness, persistence or financial outcomes.

cases.title: Progress needs an owner
cases.observation: A task view by itself does not make separation of responsibility obvious. The later scene places people beside the work.
cases.decision: Animate task assignment, individual progress and a shared meter that reaches 100 percent.
cases.why: Responsibility and completion become concrete outcomes instead of abstract project-management promises.
cases.outtake: The earlier task view is superseded for storytelling. The illustrated people and completion remain synthetic, not live proof of a finished customer job.
cases.lesson: Ask what observable behavior would substantiate the benefit headline.

cases.title: Make the example local to the buyer
cases.observation: Harris County is a plausible demo but the intended recipient is in Florida.
cases.decision: Use Hillsborough County and the stored portal/contact resources relevant to that example.
cases.why: A familiar jurisdiction reduces the mental translation from product demo to the buyer's work.
cases.outtake: Harris County is not factually wrong; it is the weaker audience match for this presentation.
cases.lesson: Separate factual correctness from relevance to the specific viewer.

cases.title: Fold details into one useful object
cases.observation: Showing county fields as separate moments consumes time and fragments a single record.
cases.decision: Unfold portal, address, email, phone and forms downward as one compact county entry.
cases.why: The viewer recognizes a reusable record, and the saved time funds a more complete service demonstration.
cases.outtake: The earlier field-by-field sequence is useful process evidence, but the final hierarchy groups related facts together.
cases.lesson: Use grouping and progressive disclosure to reclaim time without deleting the useful information.

cases.title: Fix the baseline, not just the box center
cases.observation: Visually centered glyph boxes can still produce uneven alphabetic baselines and inconsistent word spacing.
cases.decision: Use shared baselines, common column edges and one high-resolution glyph source through zooms.
cases.why: Stable letter relationships make the composition feel intentional, especially during scaling and replacement.
cases.outtake: The prior opening is retained for comparison. Baseline and encoded-pixel checks substantiate this correction beyond taste.
cases.lesson: Turn a vague alignment complaint into a measurable text-placement problem.

cases.title: Carry completion into the next scene
cases.observation: The owner identified the 100 percent completion handoff as a jump cut.
cases.decision: Fill the orange check and use that same object to travel into the next scene's dot.
cases.why: One persistent focal object lets the viewer understand the transition without reorienting.
cases.outtake: The earlier cut is an outtake for continuity, not for the meaning of completion. Compare the motion strip as well as the still.
cases.lesson: Match the endpoint position, scale and meaning across a scene boundary.

cases.title: Remove the tiny-dot detour
cases.observation: Returning from the zoom to a tiny moving circle adds a second path before the brand mark is formed.
cases.decision: Contract directly into the slash, settle it at about 13 seconds and remove the remaining perspective drift.
cases.why: The viewer follows one direct transformation into the brand, with fewer stops and less travel.
cases.outtake: The dot-matching version solved an earlier seam but became the outtake once the brief called for a more direct reveal.
cases.lesson: A technically continuous animation can still contain unnecessary attention shifts.

cases.title: Generalize only when the story widens
cases.observation: Keeping Hillsborough County on the entire organization map can make a general relationship look county-specific.
cases.decision: Retain the named close-up, then change the map label to County as the complete structure appears.
cases.why: The example stays concrete while the wider diagram communicates a reusable pattern.
cases.outtake: The named label is kept in the source version and close-up, but superseded at the general relationship stage.
cases.lesson: Control when to be specific and when to abstract.

cases.title: Turn a feature name into a payoff
cases.observation: Feature-led wording tells the viewer what is on screen. The V2 treatment pairs the problem with the payoff.
cases.decision: Move from Clear ownership to Who owns this? and Every task. An owner.; retain the visual proof underneath.
cases.why: A buyer can connect the animation to a recognizable work problem without reading a product explanation.
cases.outtake: V1 is preserved as a valid alternative direction, not erased or called a failed product.
cases.lesson: Rewrite the promise while preserving the demonstration and the established style.

cases.title: Make industry adaptability visible
cases.observation: The solar demonstration alone can make a broader workflow product feel like a single-trade offering.
cases.decision: Hold PowerPortals for fixed and flip the orange industry word through seven construction/remodeling trades.
cases.why: A stable brand prefix and changing category communicate adaptability with very little copy.
cases.outtake: The earlier invitation remains a shorter alternative. Trade names are positioning, not proof that every trade template or external CRM has been tested.
cases.lesson: Use a controlled variable to broaden relevance while keeping visual identity stable.

cases.title: Resolve audio perception with provenance
cases.observation: The owner reported that the music felt blended and supplied a fresh track.
cases.decision: Use the supplied Steady Progress WAV as the sole bed, place individual short effects separately and verify source identity.
cases.why: A clear music/effects separation makes authorship and mix changes reviewable instead of guessing at the cause of a listening impression.
cases.outtake: The previous generated score was superseded. Its source indicates one composed bed plus effects; the archive does not establish that two music beds were accidentally overlaid.
cases.lesson: Respect perceptual feedback without inventing a technical diagnosis. Listen to the linked A/B samples; these two stills intentionally match.

cases.title: Spend attention on the brand, not the footer
cases.observation: The long disclosure ending holds the large CTA while small phrases change for over twenty seconds.
cases.decision: Remove the large CTA, keep the logo central and place the revised wording in a five-second three-line footer.
cases.why: The final selected cut becomes 114 seconds instead of 134.5667, while the product remains the dominant closing image.
cases.outtake: The long version remains available for reading. The shorter footer trades full read-through time for lower attention cost; no comprehension or legal sufficiency claim is made.
cases.lesson: Record the trade-off honestly, including the owner-directed API wording and its evidence limits.

cases.title: Gather information instead of dropping it
cases.observation: The county details originally clear by fading. That disappearance does not explain why the next network grows from the county icon.
cases.decision: Turn the related text orange and gather it into the top icon before the relationship map expands.
cases.why: The transition carries the record forward as one object, maintaining a visual link between details and structure.
cases.outtake: The fading version is retained as a weaker continuity solution. The before/after timestamps differ because the edit was retimed.
cases.lesson: Use a transition to preserve information hierarchy, not merely to hide a cut.

cases.title: Let the play shape become the reply surface
cases.observation: The filled play arrow previously expands into a wipe. The revised brief calls for less travel and a dot-to-composer connection.
cases.decision: Shrink and round the triangle, land the dot at the composer position, then grow that dot into the reply box.
cases.why: The same orange object links automation, customer context and reply action without another full-screen reset.
cases.outtake: The expanding triangle remains a valid energetic wipe, but it is superseded for this more continuous handoff.
cases.lesson: Specify the destination object and its coordinates before choosing the transition gesture.
